'''''Portea petropolitana''''' is a plant [[species]] of the genus ''[[Portea]]'', in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Bromeliaceae]].

==Distribution==
The [[bromeliad]] is [[endemic]] to the [[Atlantic Forest|Atlantic Forest biome]] (''Mata Atlantica Brasileira''), located in southeastern [[Brazil]].

It is found within the states of [[Bahia]], [[Espírito Santo]], [[Minas Gerais]], and [[Rio de Janeiro (state)]]

==Description==
There are two varieties of ''Portea petropolitana'' that are cultivated as [[ornamental plant]]s:
*''Portea petropolitana'' var. ''petropolitana'' — native to [[Espírito Santo]] near the ocean. It may reach a height of 3 to 4 feet prior to flowering. The dark green leaves are heavily spined and form a stiff rosette. The inflorescence reaches 12 to 18 inches long, bearing colorful flowers with white lavender petals and orange sepals.<ref>{{cite book|last=Padilla|first=Victoria|title=Bromeliads|year=1973|publisher=Crown Publishers|location=New York|isbn=0517562413|pages=[https://archive.org/details/bromeliads00vict/page/60 60]|url=https://archive.org/details/bromeliads00vict/page/60}}</ref>
[[File:Portea Petropolitana.jpg|thumbnail|left|Portea Petropolitana growing in shade.]]
*''Portea petropolitana'' var. ''extensa'' native to [[Espírito Santo]]. Introduced by American plant collector and breeder M. B. Foster. It is smaller in all parts compared to the other variety.<ref>{{cite book|last=Rauh|first=Werner|title=Bromeliads For Home, Garden and Greenhouses|year=1979|publisher=Nlandford Press Ltd.|isbn=071370845X|pages=349}}</ref> It is characterized by light yellow green leaves and a coral red inflorescence with an upright rosette. The flower contains lavender petals, apple green overies, and berries that turn dark purple.<ref>{{cite book|last=Padilla|first=Victoria|title=Bromeliads|year=1973|publisher=Crown Publishers|location=New York|isbn=0517562413|pages=[https://archive.org/details/bromeliads00vict/page/61 61]|url=https://archive.org/details/bromeliads00vict/page/61}}</ref>
